Stare decisis, also known as "the principle of precedent," is a legal concept that means the court should follow its previous decisions when making new ones. This means that if there is already a case decided by a higher court in the same jurisdiction with similar facts or circumstances, the lower court can use those decisions as a basis for ruling on its own case.

The rationale behind this principle is that precedent helps to maintain consistency and predictability in legal judgments, which can help ensure fairness and justice. It also allows courts to save time and resources by not having to re-examine every argument or issue in each case.

However, it's important to note that the application of stare decisis depends on several factors, such as whether the case is similar enough to the precedent for the court to follow it, whether the precedent was made in a jurisdiction with different legal principles than the current one, and whether there are any new or relevant information that would change the outcome.
